title: What pattern appears when a minus b multiplies longer brackets?
description: Eigh minus b multiplies three longer and longer brackets. The middle terms cancel each time, a pattern appears, and the next case is written and checked by expanding.
teaching_notes: One idea: when eigh minus b multiplies a bracket of powers, the middle terms cancel in pairs and only two terms are left. Same method as the six pieces video in your book.

source: Expand (i) (a − b)(a + b), (ii) (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) and (iii) (a − b)(a³ + a²b + ab² + b³). Do you see a pattern? What would be the next identity in the pattern? Can you check it by expanding?
video_script.why: The child has multiplied every term by every term and added the like terms. Here the same method shows a pattern.
video_script.substitution: Expand each bracket, watch which terms cancel, read the pattern, and test the next case by expanding.
video_script.anchor: eigh minus b multiplying three longer and longer brackets
video_script.payoff_line: Only the first and last terms remain

final_answer.value: a² − b², a³ − b³, a⁴ − b⁴; next (a − b)(a⁴ + a³b + a²b² + ab³ + b⁴) = a⁵ − b⁵
final_answer.spoken: eigh squared minus b squared, eigh cubed minus b cubed, eigh to the fourth minus b to the fourth, and next eigh to the fifth minus b to the fifth

hold_back: a² − b², a³ − b³, a⁴ − b⁴; next (a − b)(a⁴ + a³b + a²b² + ab³ + b⁴) = a⁵ − b⁵
maths_rules: (a − b)(a + b) = a² + ab − ab − b² = a² − b²
(a − b)(a² + ab + b²) = a³ + a²b + ab² − a²b − ab² − b³ = a³ − b³
(a − b)(a³ + a²b + ab² + b³) = a⁴ + a³b + a²b² + ab³ − a³b − a²b² − ab³ − b⁴ = a⁴ − b⁴
pattern: (a − b) times the bracket of descending powers of a and ascending powers of b gives a^n − b^n
(a − b)(a⁴ + a³b + a²b² + ab³ + b⁴) = a⁵ + a⁴b + a³b² + a²b³ + ab⁴ − a⁴b − a³b² − a²b³ − ab⁴ − b⁵ = a⁵ − b⁵
video_script.design: One idea: terms equal with opposite signs cancel, so a long bracket collapses to two terms. Uses the method of the six pieces video. The three results stay on the board while the pattern is read.

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, take the first expression. Eigh times the bracket gives eigh squared plus eigh b.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Minus b times the bracket gives minus eigh b minus b squared.
<bookmark mark='tidy'/>Eigh b and minus eigh b cancel, leaving eigh squared minus b squared.

beats.on_screen: (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) = a³ + a²b + ab² − a²b − ab² − b³ = a³ − b³

marks.one: a × (a² + ab + b²) = a³ + a²b + ab² is written
marks.two: −b × (a² + ab + b²) = −a²b − ab² − b³ is written
marks.tidy: a²b and −a²b, ab² and −ab² are crossed out and a³ − b³ is written

beats.colours: each cancelling pair in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, take the second expression. Eigh times the bracket gives eigh cubed, plus eigh squared b, plus eigh b squared.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Minus b times the bracket gives minus eigh squared b, minus eigh b squared, minus b cubed.
<bookmark mark='tidy'/>The middle terms cancel in pairs, leaving eigh cubed minus b cubed.

beats.on_screen: (a − b)(a³ + a²b + ab² + b³) = a⁴ + a³b + a²b² + ab³ − a³b − a²b² − ab³ − b⁴ = a⁴ − b⁴

marks.one2: + a²b² + ab³ is added to it
marks.two: −b × (a³ + a²b + ab² + b³) = −a³b − a²b² is written
marks.two2: − ab³ − b⁴ is added to it
marks.tidy: the three middle pairs are crossed out and a⁴ − b⁴ is written

beats.colours: each cancelling pair in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step three, the last bracket has four terms. Eigh times it gives eigh to the fourth, plus eigh cubed b.
<bookmark mark='one2'/>Then plus eigh squared b squared, plus eigh b cubed.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Minus b times it gives minus eigh cubed b, and minus eigh squared b squared.
<bookmark mark='two2'/>Then minus eigh b cubed, and minus b to the fourth.
<bookmark mark='tidy'/>Every middle term cancels, leaving eigh to the fourth minus b to the fourth.

<bookmark mark='pow'/>The power goes up by one each time, so the next power is five.

narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step five, check the next case by expanding. The next bracket has five terms, from eigh to the fourth down to b to the fourth.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Eigh times it starts with eigh to the fifth and ends with eigh b to the fourth.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Minus b times it starts with minus eigh to the fourth times b.
It ends with minus b to the fifth.
<bookmark mark='tidy'/>Every middle term cancels again, so the result is eigh to the fifth minus b to the fifth.

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Only the first and last terms remain.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>The results are eigh squared minus b squared, and eigh cubed minus b cubed.
Then eigh to the fourth minus b to the fourth.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>The next identity multiplies eigh minus b by the five term bracket.
It equals eigh to the fifth minus b to the fifth.
